artifacts.title: Huffman v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Huffman filed an appeal after the 50th GA amended BCO 38-1 to change the remedy from complaint to appeal, but his case originated and was nearly complete under the prior rule allowing complaint. The SJC found the case judicially out of order and remanded to Tennessee Valley Presbytery to adjudicate as a complaint under the then-existing rule, resetting the clock for presbytery action.

artifacts.title: Speck v. Missouri Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained in part and denied in part TE Ryan Speck's complaint against Missouri Presbytery's December 2019 adoption of six theological judgments regarding the 2018 Revoice Conference hosted by Memorial Presbyterian Church, ruling that MOP applied an incorrect constitutional standard (BCO 34-5 'vitals of religion') rather than the proper BCO 11-3, 11-4, and 13-9(f) criteria, and failed to take adequate action with respect to erroneous teachings identified by its own committees regarding terminology (TJ 2), the 'gay beneath the gay' (TJ 3), and spiritual friendships (TJ 5); the matter was remanded to MOP with instructions for a new hearing. Dissenting opinions were filed by RE John D. Pickering and TE David F. Coffin, Jr., who argued that the SJC improperly raised an issue not presented by either party in violation of BCO 39-3.1.

artifacts.synopsis: RE Mueller complained that the Redlands Community Church Session reaffirmed a practice of fencing the Lord's Table contrary to BCO 58-4, but the SJC found the Session took no action because the relevant motion failed for lack of a second. The complaint was denied, with a concurring opinion emphasizing that BCO 58-4's fencing requirement remains a constitutional obligation.

artifacts.title: Dailey v. Heritage Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: RE Dailey complained that Heritage Presbytery erred in upholding its Moderator's ruling that a church member's document was administratively in order as a complaint under BCO 43-3, after the Session had ruled it out of order. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that neither triggering condition of BCO 43-3 was met because the Session's ruling that the document did not qualify as a BCO 43-1 complaint was not equivalent to denying it, and the Session had considered and responded to the matter in a timely manner. A substantial dissent argued for a broader interpretation of 'fails to consider' in BCO 43-3.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained the Session of FPC North Port's complaint that Southwest Florida Presbytery erred when it remanded a previously out-of-order complaint back to the Session and when it directed and instructed the Session to initiate formal ecclesiastical process against a member without following the required steps of BCO 40-5. The Commission held that once the Original CM Complaint was found out of order, there was no matter for Presbytery to carry forward, and any subsequent instructions to the Session to initiate process were null and void.

artifacts.title: the Session of Hope Community Church v. Central Carolina Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Hope Community Church complained that Central Carolina Presbytery erred in adopting a policy requiring a multi-site session to eventually particularize its second worship site as a distinct new church. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the BCO expressly vests the Session with authority over the time and place of worship and the Presbytery's mandatory particularization requirement exceeded its constitutional powers and was annulled.

A concurring opinion by RE Duncan and RE Burnett noted that JRP's commission gave de novo review beyond the Record of the Case and should have narrowly adjudicated whether JRP erred in denying the original complaint.
